name: draft_docstring
title: Draft a Waterloo docstring
description: Draft or refine a Waterloo docstring from a callable signature or an existing source object.

arguments.name: profile
arguments.description: The Waterloo profile to generate: module, class, function, method, or inherited_method.

messages.content:
Draft or refine a Waterloo docstring for a $profile object.

For a new callable known only by its signature, use `gen_docstring` with that signature as the structural starting point.

When you need an example of Authoring JSON syntax, especially for paragraphs, nested lists, tables, or profile-specific sections, first inspect the matching showcase:
`waterlint gen-showcase-authoring-json --profile $profile --out <showcase.json>`
Treat the showcase only as a syntax reference. Do not copy its placeholder identifiers, descriptions, or normative statements into the target documentation.

For an existing local object, first compare `get_signature`, `get_examples`, and `get_references` before proposing wording. Then use the Authoring JSON workflow:

1. Generate an editable starting document:
   `waterlint gen-full-authoring-json --basedir <basedir> --obj <qualified-name> --out <authoring.json>`
2. Edit the JSON's `doc` object. Write complete logical text, select paragraph, list, or table blocks where appropriate, use Waterloo pipe notation such as |Must| and |func|`some_name`, and do not add physical indentation, line wrapping, Python quote delimiters, or backslash continuations.
3. Validate the Authoring JSON:
   `waterlint validate-json --in <authoring.json>`
4. Render it deterministically:
   `waterlint render-docstring --in <authoring.json> --out <docstring.txt>`
5. Insert the rendered content as the target object's Python docstring.
6. Validate the real object:
   `waterlint validate --basedir <basedir> --obj <qualified-name>`

Use the resulting Waterlint diagnostics to improve the Authoring JSON, then repeat JSON validation, rendering, and target validation. Authoring JSON validation checks its structure and source-independent Waterloo semantics. Final validation remains necessary for source-specific concerns such as signatures, exception classes, references, scopes, and allowed sections.

Prefer normative sections over Notes when the text should state a rule.
